title: Assistant Professor of General Business - John Chambers College of Business and Economics
description:
The Department of General Business in the John Chambers College of
Business and Economics at West Virginia University (located in
Morgantown, WV) invites applications for an Assistant Professor
of General Business starting Fall 2027. The position will
involve teaching under the Department of General Business, with a
research and service affiliation to the Knee Regulatory Research
Center (KRRC) and/or Center for Free Enterprise (CFE), focusing on
topics related to the economics of regulation, business law, and
healthcare policy.

The primary teaching responsibility for this position will be
teaching courses around economics and business law with
consideration for the candidate's area of expertise. Candidates
should demonstrate a teaching philosophy that emphasizes
experiential learning and student engagement. The successful
candidate will be expected to teach effectively in both in-person
and online formats at the undergraduate and/or graduate levels, and
to collaborate with colleagues to support and strengthen the
college's innovative, student-centered culture. This position
includes a teaching load of 18 credits per year, with both service
and research dedicated to the Center for Free Enterprise and/or
Knee Regulatory Research Center.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to collaborate
with scholars within the Knee Regulatory Research Center or the
Center for Free Enterprise, both under the discretion of Dr. Alicia
Plemmons, Director of KRRC and CFE. Candidates with a Ph.D. in
economics, business law, public policy, or a related field with
research interest in regulatory or legislative analysis are
encouraged to apply. Salary and benefits will be competitive and
commensurate with experience and qualifications. The position and
start date are subject to budget approval.

Qualifications :

Qualified candidates must hold, at the time of appointment, a Ph.D.
in economics, business law, public policy, or a related field, with
demonstrated research interest in regulatory and legislative
processes at the state and/or federal level. Candidates in the
advanced stages of a Ph.D. will also be considered but must have
completed their degree before the start date of this
position.

West Virginia University (and the John Chambers College of Business
and Economics) is particularly interested in candidates who can
contribute, through their teaching and service, to the excellence
of the academic community.

Application Process

Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue
until the position is filled. Applicants must submit the following
items electronically: (1) a letter of interest, (2) curriculum
vitae, (3) a statement of teaching philosophy, (4) a writing
sample, and (5) contact information for three references.

Please submit applications electronically here .

General inquiries may be directed to Dr. Alicia Plemmons, Director
of the Knee Regulatory Research Center, Director of the Center for
Free Enterprise, and Associate Professor of General Business, at
Alicia.Plemmons@mail.wvu.edu
.
